Open to group projects. Sample resume for practice only.

Skills

  2. Help a classmate with HTML.

lessons.title: Show and Tell: Juan's Picture and Education Table

objectives.cognitive: Describe the img, audio and video elements and the table elements, attributes and values used on a resume page.
objectives.affective: Respect privacy and permission when choosing pictures for a resume.
objectives.psychomotor: Add Juan's profile picture and an education table in CodeShare and run both.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Run every sample unchanged first, then do its small task. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample into index.html; **Run code** shows the page in the page window and checks it. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then Media checks, one line for each picture, sound and video. Pictures, sound, video, alt text and list markers are not page text. In a table, each row is one line and a tab separates its cells. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 1 page carries forward in your module project. Every step this week grows the same index.html; the boxes show only the lines a step adds or changes, and where they go.
**Week 2 starts here:** Juan's Week 1 page is all words: no picture, sound or video, and his schools would be one long sentence.

img shows a picture, audio plays sound and video plays a video; each names its file with src. alt describes a picture for people who cannot see it. A table shows data in rows and columns: tr is a row, th a heading cell, td a data cell, caption the table's title; thead holds the heading rows and tbody the data rows.
A school bulletin board shows a poster with a caption under it, and a printed class schedule is a grid of rows and columns. img is the poster; a table is the grid.

rows: A video with a play button
images/, audio/ or video/, then the exact file name
The file name starts its Media checks line

blocks.instruction: Juan's Week 1 page carries forward. This step replaces the photo comment under his name with his profile picture. Press Work in code editor, then Run code without changing anything: the picture shows in the page window and Media checks says image decoded.

lessons.title: Hear and See Juan: Adding and Checking Sound and Video

objectives.cognitive: Explain the src, alt, controls and width attributes and how CodeShare checks pictures, sound and video.
objectives.affective: Value describing sound and video for classmates who cannot hear or see them.
objectives.psychomotor: Add and check Juan's sound greeting and video, then describe each one on the page.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Monday's page has a picture but no sound or video, and a file's content means nothing to a reader who cannot see or hear it.

src names the file exactly: images/, audio/ or video/, then its name, such as images/juan_profile.svg. controls shows the play button; width and height set the size in pixels; loop plays again from the start; muted starts silent. Text inside audio or video is only for very old browsers, so describe each file in a p.
A barangay announcement played on a speaker also gets a written notice, for people who did not hear it. Sound and video on a page need a written description too.

**Media steps:** every step this week shows Juan's picture, sound and video, files your teacher adds under Media files. Online, CodeShare checks them automatically; Run code waits on Loading media… until they are on this device. Offline, media cannot load yet: the step shows Checked by your teacher for now, and your teacher presses Mark done.

rows: Drawn as an SVG on the teacher's laptop; not a photo
Three title cards ending with his name, about 4 seconds, no sound
Drawn and recorded on the teacher's laptop

blocks.instruction: This step adds Juan's sound greeting: an audio element whose src names the file and whose controls attribute shows a play button. Run it unchanged, then press play in the page window.

lessons.title: Organise Juan's Data: Table Headings, Rows and Spans

objectives.cognitive: Explain th, td, caption, thead and tbody and the scope, colspan and rowspan attributes and their values.
objectives.affective: Organise data clearly so that readers can compare it quickly.
objectives.psychomotor: Build Juan's award row with colspan and a skill table with row groups and rowspan.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Monday's table lists Juan's schools, but an award line or a group of skills cannot yet stretch across cells.

scope tells which cells a th labels: col for its column, row for its row, rowgroup for the rows of its tbody. colspan makes a cell cover more than one column and rowspan more than one row; both are whole numbers and both start at 1.
On a jeepney fare matrix, one heading can cover several columns, and one route can cover several rows. colspan and rowspan do the same in a table.

rows: A whole number; 1 if left out
A whole number; 1 if left out

blocks.instruction: This step adds an award row to the Education table. It has one td with colspan="3", so the cell covers all three columns. Run it unchanged first.

performanceTask.title: My Resume, Week 2: Picture and Table
performanceTask.markdown:
Start Thursday; finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project. Your Week 1 resume carries forward: add this week's parts to it.

Add a picture and a table. The picture is your own photo (optional, with only you in it) or a picture your teacher gives you. Online, add it under Media files in your personal project: in images, with a name of letters, numbers, - and _ only, such as my_photo.jpg, at most 5 MB. Offline, Media files are not available yet: write the img now; the picture shows once the file is added online. Then add an education or skills table with a caption, th headings and at least two rows.

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or personal social-media accounts, and no other people in your picture. Run code until the page runs with no error, then press Submit this version. Saving or running is not submitting.

Thursday: 0–60 minutes, repairs and the Thursday strip; 60–120 minutes, plan on paper, show the teacher, then start. Friday: 0–30 minutes, finish and run; 30–105 minutes, five-minute presentations; 105–120 minutes, Friday strip and Submit this version.
checklist: Keep your Week 1 page: your name in h1, your introduction and your lists.
Add one img with src in images/, an alt that describes it, and width and height.
Use your own photo (only you in it) or your teacher's picture, added under Media files online.
Write a visible sentence that describes your picture.
Add an education or skills table with a caption.
Put the headings in th with scope="col", inside thead.
Add at least two rows of td inside tbody.
Use colspan or rowspan once, for example an award row.
No home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or social media; no other people in the picture.
Run code shows no error; press Submit this version, then present.
